name: The Hollow Choir (Resonance Flash Phenomenon)
description: Approximately every eleven weeks, somewhere in the Meridian 88 transit corridor, a group of between forty and three hundred people simultaneously stop walking, tilt their heads back, and produce a sustained harmonic tone for exactly ninety seconds before dispersing without acknowledgment or explanation. Participants later report no memory of the event but describe a sense of profound resonance — a feeling that something was 'tuning' them. Acoustic engineers who have recorded the phenomenon note the chord produced is not achievable by unaugmented human vocal cords and contains subsonic elements that affect nearby BCI users. The phenomenon has been documented in transit hubs, pedestrian bridges, and twice inside Vantabloc Corporation's Tier 4 atrium, which caused significant corporate alarm.
cultural_impact: The Hollow Choir has generated a devoted community of observers who call themselves Resonance Chasers, using predictive algorithms to anticipate the next occurrence and gathering at likely sites. It has also seeded genuine public anxiety about BCI security, with several corponations quietly issuing firmware patches they claim are unrelated to the phenomenon.
key_figures: Unknown — no one has identified an originating agent
story_hooks: A Resonance Chaser has developed an algorithm that predicts the next Hollow Choir occurrence with 94% accuracy — and someone is willing to pay an enormous sum to suppress that prediction before it can be published.

A character who participated in a Hollow Choir event begins hearing a faint continuation of the tone in their BCI feed at random moments, and the subsonic element is slowly changing their behavior in ways they cannot detect.
An E.L.F. contacts a journalist claiming to be the origin of the Hollow Choir and offering to explain — but the explanation turns out to be something no human institution wants made public.
